overview_summary: 401 W 6th Street is a 52-unit, four-story elevator apartment building in the heart of Downtown Long Beach (built 1974). The location is a standout: a Walk Score of 87, three blocks from Pine Avenue, and roughly a third of a mile from the Metro A Line — in a submarket riding a multi-billion-dollar development wave and benefitting from California's most landlord-favorable regulatory posture among major LA-area cities (no local rent control).
rent_summary: Downtown Long Beach is the city's strongest rent submarket, with a median asking rent around $2,460 — about 26% above the national average. The figures below reflect current area asking rents by unit type and at competing communities.

investment_highlights: Walker's-paradise-adjacent location — Walk Score 87 (Very Walkable), ~0.3 mi to the Metro A Line at Pacific Ave Station and three blocks to Pine Avenue's dining and nightlife.
No local rent control — Long Beach repealed its local ordinance in 2019 and relies solely on California's AB 1482, giving owners more rent-growth flexibility than nearby City of Los Angeles assets.

Riding a $10B+ downtown development wave: LA County's largest waterfront amphitheater (opening 2026), the $200M Alexan West End (largest residential project in the city), and 5,200+ units approved 2023–2025.
52 units offers professional, scalable ownership with a deep private-capital and 1031 buyer pool in a supply-constrained infill submarket.
Classic 1974 vintage in the city's top rent submarket implies a likely gap between in-place and market rents — a clear value-add lever on turnover.

regulations.title: No Local Rent Control
regulations.impact: Long Beach repealed its local Tenant Relocation Assistance Ordinance in December 2019 and has no local rent-stabilization board. Compared with the City of Los Angeles, this is a meaningful relative advantage for rent growth and value.

regulations.title: California AB 1482 (Statewide Cap)
regulations.impact: Covered units are limited to 5% + local CPI, capped at 10%. For increases effective Aug 1, 2025–Jul 31, 2026 the Long Beach-area maximum is 8%. Provides a predictable growth floor that applies to competing product as well.

regulations.title: Just Cause for Eviction
regulations.impact: Long Beach follows AB 1482's just-cause provisions; relocation assistance may apply for no-fault terminations. Factor turnover timing into any aggressive reposition plan.

regulations.title: Verify Occupancy Designation
regulations.impact: Some listings reference operation under the Housing for Older Persons Act (55+). Confirm the property's actual designation — it materially affects the tenant pool, marketing, and applicable protections.
